messages.content: i got home early today. i keep thinking i must have something left to do because there is still so much afternoon left.
coming home early can feel different from what you do most days. do you know that the work you needed to finish is done, or is there one thing you want to check?
i checked my work already, and it is done.
then you have checked the part that worried you. you can choose how to use this time without making another task just because the afternoon is open.
i want to sit outside, but i feel like that is doing nothing.
sitting outside can be what you choose to do with free time. it does not need to make something for it to be a good part of your day.
can you ask me something about outside instead of work?
where would you like to sit?
there is a chair near a tree in the garden. i can hear people in the street from there.
then you have a place to sit with a little of the world around you. would you like to take a drink or just go as you are?
just go. i do not want another thing to get ready.
that keeps it simple. the chair and a little time outside are enough for the plan you chose.
write a story about a child making a small model of a house with his uncle. the child should choose one detail himself.

a child and his uncle sit at a table to make a small house. the uncle helps with the wall and roof, but asks the child where the window should go. the child chooses the side near a toy tree. he wants the person inside the model to see leaves. when the house is ready, he puts his eye near the window and looks through. he can see the tree, just as he wanted. his uncle asks if they need another window, and the child says he wants to think before choosing.
use wanted in the sentence about seeing the tree.
he can see the tree, just as he wanted.
did the uncle choose every part?
no. he helped with the wall and roof, but the child chose the place for the window. the story leaves room for both people to help.
why might the child want to think before adding another window?
he may want to see how the first one works in the little house before changing it. the story does not have to give an answer right away.
make the last part a short conversation.
do you want another window? not yet. i want to look through this one again first. okay. we can choose the next part later.
write a conversation where two people both want soup, but one wants a small cup and the other wants more.
would you like soup? yes, just a small cup, please. i would like a larger cup. are you both hungry? i am only a little hungry. i have not had lunch, so i would like more.
who has not had lunch?
the person asking for the larger cup. the other person said they were only a little hungry.
can both say yes to the same question and still want different things?
yes. both want soup, but one wants a small cup and the other wants a larger one. saying yes to the food does not choose every detail about the meal.
answer simply.
yes. both want soup, but one wants a small cup and the other wants a larger one.
now make the person who asked for a small cup ask for more later.
that was good, thank you. could i have a little more soup?
does that make the first request a lie?
no. someone can want a small cup at first and choose more after eating it. the later choice does not by itself tell us that the first request was false.
make that last idea simple.
no. a person can ask for a small cup first and want more later.
my friend and i chose to meet at the park tomorrow. i forgot the hour. help me ask only about that detail.
what time did we choose to meet at the park tomorrow?
can you leave out park and tomorrow if those are already clear in the conversation?
yes. you can ask: what time did we choose to meet?
why not ask do you still want to meet?
that asks about whether the meeting is still wanted, rather than the hour you forgot. it could be useful in another context, but it is not the detail you said you need.
write a reply if my friend says three, and three works for me.
three works for me. i will see you then.
if i say i forgot the hour, does that mean we had no plan before?
no. you had a plan, but you do not remember one part. you are asking for that part again.
answer simply.
no. you can have a plan and need to ask for one detail again.
i see two animals in a garden. then one leaves, and another comes in. are there still two animals?
yes, if one animal is still there while one leaves and one new animal comes in. the number is still two, even though one of the animals is different.
use is still there in a simple answer.
yes. one animal is still there, and one new animal comes in after the other leaves. there are two again.
are the same two animals still there?
no. the number is the same, but the whole group is not. one of the first two left, and a different animal came in.
ask my last question simply.
are the same two animals still in the garden?
write a story with a child who sees that difference.

a child watches two animals in a garden. one walks out through the door, and another comes in. her brother says there are still two. she says yes, but one is new. they watch the animal still there and see that it has not moved.
say my story request simply.
write a story with a child who sees that the number is the same but one animal is new.
i found a letter from an old friend and want to write back, but it has been a long time. i do not know if they still live in the same place.
you can begin by saying you found the letter and would like to hear from them. before sending it, you may need to check how to reach them now.
write a short message without saying i know where they live.
i found your old letter today and wanted to write. i hope we can talk again. what is a good way for us to talk now?
use talk in the question.
i found your old letter today and wanted to write. i hope we can talk again. what is a good way for us to talk now?
should i say sorry because i did not write before now?
you can if that is something you want to say. you do not have to give a reason you do not remember or make up a story about why you did not write.
make my question simple.
should i say sorry because i did not write before now?
can the message still be kind without a long reason?
yes. a simple wish to talk again can be kind. you can leave the longer story for another conversation if both of you want it.
i like quiet music while i clean, but my brother is trying to read in the same room. help me ask what works for both of us.
you could say: would quiet music be okay while i clean, or would it make reading hard for you?
he says even quiet music makes it hard today.
then you have useful information about what he needs today. you could clean without music for now or choose a different room if that is possible.
i cannot clean another room because this is the room that needs cleaning.
then this is the room that needs the work. you can clean without music now or ask about a time when he will read in another room.
use another room in a simple answer.
you could ask when he plans to read in another room, or clean without music now.
i will clean quietly now. write my reply.
okay. i will leave the music off while i clean today.
does that mean i never get to play music again?
no. this is a choice for today while your brother reads. a plan for one part of one day does not have to become a rule for every day.
my child wants to send a drawing to her grandmother. she asked me to write what it is, but she does not want a long story.
ask her what she wants her grandmother to know first. she may want to name the things in the picture or say why she drew them.
she says it is the garden we visited, with a tree in the middle.
you could write: this is the garden we visited. i drew the tree in the middle because i liked it.
she did not say why she put the tree there.
then keep that reason out: this is the garden we visited, with the tree in the middle.
can we add that she wants to go again if she says yes?
yes. if that is her own idea, you can add: i would like to go there again.
she says yes. put the message together.
this is the garden we visited, with the tree in the middle. i would like to go there again.
what if i think she liked the flowers more than the tree?
you can ask her rather than choosing that feeling for her. the message should keep the idea she wants to share.
i told you my book is on the shelf. now i ask if it could be on the desk. did i tell you i moved it?
no. you asked about another place, but did not give a new fact about moving it. the last place you said it was is the shelf.
answer simply.
no. asking about the desk does not say that you moved the book there. the shelf is the place you gave.
now i say i moved it to the desk this morning. where is it?
on the desk, using the new detail you gave.
what if i ask whether my sister moved it again?
that is a question, rather than information that she did. i should not say she moved it until you give that detail.
can you ask me a useful question instead?
do you know whether your sister moved the book after you put it on the desk?
i do not know.
then the desk is still the last place you know it was. you can check there first, but we do not know whether it is still there now.
i want to make breakfast easy tomorrow. i have bread and milk, but i have not chosen what to have.
you already have a few things to work with. do you want to choose now or just make sure they are ready for the morning?
i want to choose now so i do not spend time thinking tomorrow.
then choose something simple from what you know you have. you could have bread with a cup of milk if that is what you enjoy.
i also have cheese. i want bread with cheese and milk to drink.
then your plan can be: have bread with cheese and a cup of milk tomorrow morning. you can put the things you need in a place that is easy to find.
should i say that is what i always have for breakfast?
not from one plan. you chose it for tomorrow. that does not tell us what you have every morning.
write a short note with only the plan for tomorrow.
tomorrow morning: bread with cheese and a cup of milk.
can you make it a full sentence?
i will have bread with cheese and a cup of milk tomorrow morning.
a teacher gives one child a picture and another child a story to explain the same idea. does that mean the answer has changed?
not always. the same idea can be explained with different examples. the important question is whether both examples keep the meaning, rather than whether they look the same.
write my question simply.
a teacher gives different examples to two children. does that mean the answer has changed?
make an example about three cups.
one child looks at a picture of three cups. another listens to a story about two cups on a desk and one brought from the kitchen. both can learn that two and one make three.
use listens to for the other child.
another child listens to a story about two cups on a desk and one brought from the kitchen. both can learn that two and one make three.
what would make one example wrong?
if a story says two cups and one more make four, that answer is wrong. different examples still need to keep the facts correct.
give a simple example with a wrong answer.
if a story says two cups and one more make four, that answer is wrong.
make my last request simple.
give a simple example with a wrong answer.
picoboi, i want you to help with a note, but ask only one question at a time.
what do you want the note to say?
that i will be late.
who will read the note?
my sister. we were going to read together at the library.
do you know how much later you will be?
no. i want to say i do not know yet.
then you could write: i will be late to the library. i do not know how much later yet, but i will tell you when i can.
can you make it kind without saying sorry again and again?
i am sorry i will be late to the library. i do not know how much later yet, but i will tell you when i can.
say my last request simply.
make it kind without saying sorry again and again.
why did you ask about the time instead of making up an hour?
you had not told me how late you would be. asking helped me keep the note to what you know.
